title: ALAASKA
expansion: Adaptive Learning for All through AI-Powered Student Knowledge Assessment
summary: Supporting independent problem solving through guided AI conversations, adaptive hints, and visible student reasoning.
research:
ALAASKA studies how conversational AI can support learning while keeping students actively involved in solving problems. Embedded in course assignments, the platform uses questions, hints, explanations, and reflection prompts to help learners articulate their ideas, examine mistakes, and revise their reasoning. Its classroom use provides a setting for studying responsible AI assistance in authentic computing and engineering education.

Our research examines how students engage with this support, when assistance helps or interrupts their work, and what their conversations reveal beyond a submitted answer. Related studies investigate student-requested and proactively offered hints, the transfer of reasoning responsibility between students and AI, and how students respond to opportunities to accept or decline help.

ALAASKA also connects student, grader, and instructor workflows. Students develop and select their responses through dialogue, while educators can review the associated reasoning process. We study how this evidence can support feedback, assessment, and instructional decisions, with independent problem solving and responsible AI use as central goals.
